title: Indian Gold and Silver ETFs Fall Up to 2.3% as Import Duty Cut Speculation Grips Market
excerpt: Gold and silver exchange-traded funds in India tumbled Thursday even as global prices held steady, as investors priced in a possible rollback of import duties from 15% to 6%.
body:
• Indian gold ETFs fell 1.3–2.3% and silver ETFs dropped 1.2–2.3% on Thursday, diverging sharply from steady global prices.
  • The Indian government is discussing a possible cut in precious metal import duties from 15% back toward 6%, according to Moneycontrol.
  • Domestic gold discounts widened by 1–1.5 percentage points as physical buyers held off purchases pending policy clarity.
  • The 15% import duty was imposed on May 13, 2026, to curb gold imports and protect foreign exchange reserves.

Gold and silver exchange-traded funds in India fell sharply on Thursday, with declines of up to 2.3%, even as global precious metal prices remained largely unchanged — a rare divergence driven entirely by domestic policy speculation.

Gold ETFs dropped between 1.3% and 2.3% at Thursday's close, while silver ETFs declined 1.2–2.3%. In the international spot market, gold was trading flat at $4,594 an ounce, and silver edged up 0.1% to $68.18 an ounce. On the MCX, gold futures were down 0.8% at around ₹1.58 lakh per 10 grams, while silver futures slipped 0.2% to ₹2.38 lakh per kilogram.

What Is Driving the Selloff

The trigger was a Moneycontrol report that discussions are underway within the central government on scaling back import duties on gold and silver. Bullion traders and jewellery industry representatives are reportedly pushing for duties to be reduced from the current 15%, with a cut to 6% being discussed. No final decision has been taken.

"The divergence between Indian and global gold and silver prices, and their ETFs, was primarily driven by the market anticipating a potential cut in import duties."

— Anindya Banerjee, Head of Currency & Commodity Research, Kotak Securities

Banerjee noted that while the duty may not be reduced all the way back to 6%, even a partial reduction could weigh on domestic prices. A cut would make gold and silver cheaper in India even if global prices remain unchanged, and ETFs that track domestic prices fell in anticipation.

Physical Market Freezes Up

The speculation has frozen India's physical gold market. Earlier this week, domestic gold was trading at a discount of around 2–2.5% to the landed or import-parity price, equivalent to roughly $45 an ounce. Overnight, that discount widened by an additional 1–1.5 percentage points.

Bhavik Patel, senior commodity analyst at Tradebulls Securities, described the reaction as classic wait-and-see behaviour. "If a duty cut lands, the landed cost of gold drops overnight," Patel said, adding that dealers holding inventory bought at the higher duty could be forced to discount further to remain competitive.

Patel said the widening is largely speculation-driven with no policy confirmation yet. "If a duty cut is announced, the domestic market could see a rapid repricing. If the government does not announce a cut, the discount could gradually return towards the mid-2% range," he said.

How the Duty Got Here

India raised import duties on gold and silver to 15% on May 13, 2026 — comprising a 10% basic customs duty and 5% agriculture infrastructure and development cess — up from the earlier 6%. The move came as part of broader efforts to curb overseas purchases of precious metals and ease pressure on the country's foreign exchange reserves. India's gold import bill had surged to approximately $72 billion in FY26, accounting for over 9% of total imports.

The duty hike had an immediate impact on domestic prices and investor behaviour. Gold ETF inflows slowed in May, and India's total gold ETF holdings dipped 0.4% month-on-month to 116.3 tonnes, according to the World Gold Council. However, the structural demand for gold investment in India — driven by a 68% price surge in FY26 — has remained resilient.

Among the Biggest ETFs

Nippon India ETF Gold BeES, the largest gold ETF by asset size, declined 1.75% on Thursday. It has gained 9.6% in the past month and 18.1% year-to-date. Nippon India Silver ETF, the largest in its segment, fell 1.6% and has returned 6.3% in the past month and 5.1% year-to-date.

Apurva Sheth, head of research at Samco Securities, said the import duties were introduced amid currency weakness, and with conditions now normalising, the government may consider rolling them back.

What to Watch

Technical analysts see gold resistance at ₹1,60,725–1,64,060, with key short-term support at ₹1,53,737 on the 100-EMA four-hourly chart. For silver, support sits at ₹2,35,700, with resistance at ₹2,43,700–2,51,000.

The divergence between Indian and global prices is expected to persist until the government provides clarity on the duty question. Analysts note that India has repeatedly tried to curb gold imports through tariff changes — most recently cutting duties from 15% to 6% in 2024 to combat smuggling — and market participants are now betting the cycle may be repeating.
